english: Sky Father, giver of goods. You who set (lit. who set, 2sg) a famous name for Dawn. You who set for us bright love/delight. You stretched out above us, you king of the gods. Hear us, hear our words. Protect our living creatures and the cattle.
uncertain: h2uséy read as dat. of Dawn, could be loc. 'at dawn'
lewbʰéh2 léwkm̥ = 'bright love/desire'? sense unclear (accusative adj. léwkm̥ is masc/fem acc., fits fem. noun)
dʰewséh2 read as collective 'breathing beings / livestock'
péh2wr̥ is 'fire', not cattle: 'protect the creatures and the fire'

english: From the nights (?) and Dawn, the great sister. Night ... and the Lady follow her (dual). You are red, and the sheep stand. And you, Night, bear the darkness. Lady, you bear bright love/light. Two sisters, protect us at night.
uncertain: nékʷtbʰos (dat./abl. pl.) at the head where a nominative 'Night' is expected; looks like a case error
h1rudʰéh1si 2sg stative 'you are red' has no clear addressee
méǵh2ih2 swésōr singular apposition to a pair

english: Night and Dawn were two sisters. Night was going into the earth. Then Dawn followed her own sister, and she was red and young. Night saw her coming and fled. The two sisters did not know each other (never met).

Young woman, who are you that come out of the sky? She is Dawn, the bright goddess. Where does she go and where does she stand? She goes and the sheep follow her. Who saw her first? The herdsman saw her first. May the bright goddess shine for us.
uncertain: kʷís masculine for a feminine referent
h2óweyes (o-grade) vs h2éweyes elsewhere in the batch

english: Sun, eye of the sky, you who know the hearts of men; who yoke the swift horses, who warm the living creatures; who melt the snow, who ripen the grain. Shine on us again, give us light.

It grows dark and night comes. Sun, you have sunk down into the water. Father, protect us from the nights. May we lie down and may sleep take us. May the dog guard our bed. May Perkunos drive/protect us. May we wake and see the light again.
uncertain: nékʷtbʰos abl. pl. 'from the nights' vs expected singular
